subject: math
title: The Equal Sign: True or False and Missing Numbers
seo_title: Grade 1 Equal Sign Worksheets: True or False Equations and Missing Numbers
standard_text: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false. For example, which of the following equations are true and which are false? 6 = 6, 7 = 8 − 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 equal sign worksheets: learn that = means “the same as” with balance scales, decide if equations are true or false, and find missing numbers like 8 + ? = 11 and 5 = ? − 3. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: The = sign means “the same as.” Both sides must have the same value.
key_sub: 7 = 8 − 1 is true because both sides are 7. 4 + 1 = 5 + 2 is false because 5 is not 7. To find a missing number, make both sides the same: 3 + 4 = 2 + 5.
body_html:
The = sign means “the same as”

The = sign does not mean “the answer comes next.” It means the same as. The two sides of = must have the same value. Think of a balance scale. When both sides are the same, the scale is level.

True or false?

Find the value of each side. If both sides are the same, the number sentence is true. If they are not, it is false.

Number sentenceLeft sideRight sideTrue or false?
6 = 666True
7 = 8 − 177True
5 + 2 = 2 + 577True
4 + 1 = 5 + 257False

Find the missing number

A ? stands for a number you do not know. Find the number that makes both sides the same.

Example

15 − ? = 9

Think addition: 9 + ? = 15. 9 + 6 = 15.

Answer: 6

Example

5 = ? − 3

Start with ?, take away 3, and 5 is left. So ? is 5 + 3 = 8. Check: 8 − 3 = 5.

Answer: 8

Numbers on both sides

Sometimes both sides have a + or a −. Find the side you know first.

Example

3 + 4 = ? + 5

The left side is 3 + 4 = 7. Now 5 + ? = 7. Count up from 5: 6, 7.

Answer: 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing the answer right after =: 3 + 4 = ? + 5 → 7Make both sides the same: 7 = 2 + 5, so ? = 2
Adding all the numbers: 8 + ? = 11 → 19Ask: 8 and what make 11? Count up from 8: 9, 10, 11. ? = 3
Saying 4 + 1 = 5 + 2 is true because 4 + 1 = 5Look at the whole right side: 5 + 2 is 7, not 5. It is false
Saying 7 = 8 − 1 is false because the answer is firstThe = sign can come first. 7 and 8 − 1 are both 7. It is true
Counting the start number: 8 + ? = 11 → 4Start at 8 and count the next numbers: 9, 10, 11. That is 3

faq.q: What does the equal sign mean in 1st grade math?
faq.a: The equal sign means “the same as.” Both sides must have the same value, so 7 = 8 − 1 and 5 + 2 = 2 + 5 are true (Common Core 1.OA.D.7).

faq.q: How do you know if a number sentence is true or false?
faq.a: Find the value of each side. If both sides are the same, it is true; if not, it is false. 4 + 1 = 5 + 2 is false because 5 is not 7.

faq.q: How do first graders find a missing number like 8 + ? = 11?
faq.a: Start at 8 and count up to 11: 9, 10, 11. That is 3 counts, so the missing number is 3. For 15 − ? = 9, think addition: 9 + 6 = 15, so it is 6.

faq.q: Why does my child write 7 for 3 + 4 = ? + 5?
faq.a: Many children think the answer always comes right after the = sign. Show a balance scale: 3 + 4 is 7, so the right side must also be 7, and 2 + 5 = 7, so the missing number is 2.

sets.title: Word problems with a missing number

items.q: Jack has 7 shells. He needs 12 shells. How many more shells does he need?
items.e: Think: 7 + ? = 12. Count up from 7 to 12: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 5. 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q: Kai has 9 stickers. He gets some more. Now he has 13 stickers. How many stickers did he get?
items.e: Think: 9 + ? = 13. Count up from 9 to 13: 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 4. 9 + 4 = 13.

items.q: Some birds are in a tree. 6 more birds come. Now there are 15 birds. How many birds were in the tree at first?
items.e: Think: ? + 6 = 15. Take away the 6 that came: 15 − 6 = 9. Check: 9 + 6 = 15.

items.q: Nora had 16 grapes. She ate some. Now she has 10 grapes. How many grapes did she eat?
items.e: Think: 16 − ? = 10. Count up from 10 to 16: 10 + 6 = 16. So the answer is 6. Check: 16 − 6 = 10.

items.q: Some kids are at the park. 4 kids go home. Now 8 kids are at the park. How many kids were at the park at first?
items.e: Think: ? − 4 = 8. Put back the 4 kids who left: 8 + 4 = 12. Check: 12 − 4 = 8.

items.q: A box holds 10 crayons. There are 7 crayons in it now. How many more crayons fit in the box?
items.e: The box holds 10. 7 are in it. Count up from 7 to 10: 8, 9, 10. That is 3. 7 + 3 = 10.

items.q: Owen wants to read 17 pages. He has read 8 pages. How many more pages does he need to read?
items.e: Think: 8 + ? = 17. From 8 to 10 is 2. From 10 to 17 is 7. 2 + 7 = 9. So 8 + 9 = 17.

items.q: Maya has 13 toy cars. She gives some to Ruby. Now Maya has 5 toy cars. How many toy cars did she give?
items.e: Think: 13 − ? = 5. Count up from 5 to 13: 5 + 8 = 13. So the answer is 8. Check: 13 − 8 = 5.

items.q: There are 10 ducks. Some ducks are in the water. 6 ducks are on the grass. How many ducks are in the water?
Zoe has 8 marbles. Emma has 3 marbles. How many more marbles does Zoe have than Emma?
items.e: Think: 3 + ? = 8. Count up from 3: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. That is 5 more.

items.q: A plate has 6 cookies. Dad puts some more on it. Now there are 14 cookies. How many cookies did Dad put on?
items.e: Think: 6 + ? = 14. From 6 to 10 is 4. From 10 to 14 is 4. 4 + 4 = 8. So 6 + 8 = 14.

items.q: There are 18 children in a class. 9 are boys. The rest are girls. How many girls are there?
Eli has some stamps. Sam gives him 7 more. Now Eli has 17 stamps. How many stamps did Eli have at first?
items.e: Think: ? + 7 = 17. Take away the 7 that came: 17 − 7 = 10. Check: 10 + 7 = 17.

items.q: Ben needs 20 points to win a game. He has 12 points. How many more points does he need?
Grace has 5 red blocks and 3 blue blocks. Luis has 6 blocks. How many more blocks does Luis need to have as many as Grace?
items.e: Grace has 5 + 3 = 8 blocks. Think: 6 + ? = 8. Count up from 6: 7, 8. That is 2. 5 + 3 = 6 + 2.

items.q: Omar has 4 red apples and 4 green apples. Jack has 2 red apples and some green apples. They have the same number of apples. How many green apples does Jack have?
items.e: Omar has 4 + 4 = 8 apples. Jack must have 8 too. Think: 2 + ? = 8. 2 + 6 = 8, so 6. 4 + 4 = 2 + 6.

items.q: Kai has 7 shells. He needs 12. Which number sentence fits?
items.e: He has 7 and needs 12 in all. 7 and some more make 12: 7 + ? = 12.

items.q: There are 15 frogs. Some hop away. 9 frogs are left. Which number sentence fits?
items.e: Start with 15. Some hop away, so take away. 9 are left: 15 − ? = 9.

items.q: Nora has some pens. She gets 4 more. Now she has 11. Which number sentence fits?
items.e: She starts with some pens. That is ?. Then 4 more come, and the total is 11: ? + 4 = 11.

items.q: Ava has 6 big bears and 2 small bears. Lily has 8 bears. Which number sentence shows they have the same?
items.e: Ava has 6 + 2 bears. Lily has 8. The same number goes on each side: 6 + 2 = 8.
